summary: Reproduced the reported VTO infinite-spin bug end-to-end on the preview URL. The widget DOES visibly open (its own branded overlay with 'xoFit' logo + close X appears), but then spins forever internally with NO toast ever appearing - confirming the new timeout/catch defensive wrapper in Fit.jsx does NOT fix the user-reported issue. Root cause identified: openVTO()/triggerVtoOpen() wraps widget.open() with a 15s timeout+catch, but widget.open()'s Promise resolves as soon as the modal SHELL is displayed (fast, ~1s) - it does not wait for the internal Banuba SDK/camera pipeline to finish loading. So `settled=true` fires almost immediately and the timer is cleared long before the real hang (which happens inside the vendor's own shadow-DOM/canvas init) ever completes or fails. The outer JS-level guard is monitoring the wrong promise. Regression checks (tab switching core/mobile/frame/core, other 4 pages) all passed cleanly with 0 relevant console errors.

ui_bugs.issue: Widget visibly opens (branded overlay + close button) but then hangs on an infinite spinner INSIDE the widget's own UI with no toast/error ever shown to the user. Reproduced twice, once with camera permission pre-granted via page.context.grant_permissions to rule out a permission-prompt block. All vendor network requests (widget.js, app.js, config.json, styles.css, translates/en.json, BanubaSDK.simd wasm/data, and ~25 other JS chunk assets) returned HTTP 200. No 4xx/5xx observed. No console errors/warnings were logged by the page or the widget at any point during the 20s+ hang.

integration_issues.issue: The timeout/catch wrapper added to Fit.jsx guards widget.open()'s own Promise, but that Promise resolves quickly once the modal shell renders - it does not track whether the widget's internal camera/SDK pipeline actually finishes loading. As a result the 15s VTO_OPEN_TIMEOUT_MS timer is cleared almost immediately (settled=true fires on open() resolution) and the user is left with exactly the same silent infinite spinner as before the fix, just rendered inside the vendor's own overlay instead of on our button. The fix does not address the reported bug.

action_items: openVTO() fix does not resolve the reported bug - widget.open()'s promise resolves on modal-shell-render, not on actual VTO/camera pipeline completion, so the 15s timeout+catch guard fires too early/never catches the real hang. Need a different detection strategy, e.g.: (1) poll for visible loading/error state inside the widget's shadow DOM (if accessible) after N seconds and force-close+toast if still spinning, or (2) listen for a vendor-emitted ready/error custom event if the Tint SDK dispatches one (check Tint/Banuba docs for onReady/onError callbacks/events), or (3) contact vendor support since assets all load fine (200) yet the SDK never finishes initializing - may be a vendor-side WASM/camera-init issue independent of our code.

Consider adding a visible manual 'Close' affordance is already present (the vendor's own X button was visible in the stuck overlay) - verify clicking that X actually closes/resets state cleanly and doesn't leave vtoLoading or any React state stuck (not fully tested here since our button itself never re-entered a loading state in this flow).
critical_code_review_comments: triggerVtoOpen(widget) assumes widget.open() returning a resolved Promise means the try-on experience is usable; that assumption is false based on live reproduction - open() only awaits the overlay mount, not readiness.
No mechanism exists to detect a hang AFTER the widget has visibly opened (e.g. MutationObserver on the widget's shadowRoot, or a vendor onReady/onError event listener) - this is the missing piece.
Regression fix from iteration_8 (persistent <tint-vto> outside AnimatePresence) is still solid - confirmed no remount/duplication issues across 4 tab switches in this run.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Reproduction steps that work reliably: goto /xofit-frame-fitting, dismiss cookie banner (button text 'Decline All' or 'Accept All'), click [data-testid='fit-tab-frame'], click [data-testid='vto-trigger-button'], wait ~5-20s. Widget overlay opens within ~1s (screenshot confirms 'xoFit' branded fullscreen overlay with close X) but shows an infinite spinner with no further progress, and no toast ever fires. Tried both with and without pre-granting camera permission via page.context.grant_permissions - same result both times, so this is not solely a getUserMedia prompt-blocking issue in headless mode (though real-user camera behavior on the live Netlify site could still differ). All ~30 vendor network requests captured returned 200, no CORS/403. Button itself (React state) never got stuck - it went straight from idle to idle without ever visibly entering the Loader2 spinner state because window.customElements.get('tint-vto') was already true (widget script already loaded from a previous test run in the same browser context in one script; worth re-testing 100% first-load-cold-cache scenario too). Tab switch regression (core/mobile/frame/core) = 0 console errors, panels all render. Other page smoke test (Home, System, xoIris, xoExam, xoLab) all returned 200 with 0 relevant console errors except one unrelated pre-existing React DOM warning ('fetchpriority' vs 'fetchPriority' prop casing) on the Home page, not related to VTO.
rca_of_the_issue: The vendor's <tint-vto> web component's .open() method resolves its Promise as soon as its own modal/overlay is mounted to the DOM (fast operation, <1s), NOT when the underlying Banuba SDK/WASM camera pipeline finishes initializing and is ready for try-on (this second phase is what visibly hangs with an infinite spinner in the reproduction). Fit.jsx's new triggerVtoOpen() wraps only the first phase's Promise with a 15s timeout+catch, so 'settled=true' fires almost immediately (well before the real hang begins), the timeout is cleared preemptively, and the user is left staring at the vendor's own silent spinner exactly as before the code change - just now displayed inside the opened overlay rather than on the trigger button. This is a logic gap in the fix, not a vendor CDN/network/CORS issue (all vendor assets returned 200 consistently across 2 separate test runs).
